ISRAEL'S MESSENGER, April 3,
1939: With the current, passover
issue, the Israel's Messenger cele-
brates its 36th anniversary. The
issue under review deals with a
wide variety of affairs and topics
of significance not only to Jews
alone.
Interesting feature is an article by
Joseph M. Levinson, a rewrite of a
Spanish writer's article in a Yiddish
newspaper in Mexico, attempting to
prove the Jewish descent of General
Francisco Franco, head of Rebel
Spain, who owes recent victory in
the civil war to Aryan Adolf Hitler
and the increasingly anti-Semitic
Mussolini.
The journal also reprints an ar-
ticle entitled "Anti-Semitism—A
World Danger," from Time and Tide
of August 6, 1938, issue. An extract
from this article follows:
"Adolf Hitler is typical of the
lowest species of anti-Semite. The
concentrated malignance of his
vengeful nature crystallizes around
a monstrous caricature which he
calls 'The Jew.' This caricature has
nothing to do with any objective
reality: it is the projection of
Hitler's own self, and those who
read Mein Kampf with care will
find that all Hitler says of the Jews
is true not of them, but of him: 'It
would be well worth while to collect
from his speeches and from Mein
Kampf all his references to the Jews
and string them together; the re-
sult would be a vivid and terribly
accurate piece of self-portraiture, a
true picture of Hitler's inner
being.'"

《以色列信使报》，1939年4月3日：随着本期逾越节特刊的发行，《以色列信使报》庆祝其创刊36周年。本期评论的内容涉及广泛的事务和话题，其重要性不仅限于犹太人。
其中有趣的一篇是约瑟夫·M·莱文森（Joseph M. Levinson）的文章，该文改写自墨西哥一家意第绪语报纸上的一位西班牙作家的文章，试图证明叛军西班牙首领弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥将军（General Francisco Franco）具有犹太血统，而佛朗哥在内战中的近期胜利要归功于雅利安人阿道夫·希特勒和日益反犹的墨索里尼。
该期刊还转载了1938年8月6日一期《时代与潮流》（Time and Tide）中题为“反犹主义——世界性危险”的一篇文章。以下是该文章的摘录：
“阿道夫·希特勒是最低劣的反犹主义者的典型。他复仇本性中集中的恶意凝结成一个他称之为‘犹太人’的怪诞漫画形象。这种漫画形象与任何客观现实都无关：它是希特勒自我的投射，那些仔细阅读《我的奋斗》的人会发现，希特勒关于犹太人的所有言论，真实的对象不是他们，而是他自己：‘如果把他演讲中和《我的奋斗》里所有提及犹太人的地方收集起来并串联在一起，那将是一幅生动且极其准确的自画像，真实地展现了希特勒的内心世界。’”

Deutsches Reich

BEKANNTMACHUNG
über die Volksabstimmung und
die Wahl zu dem grossdeutschen
Reichstag am 10. April 1938.

AN DER Volksabstimmung über
die Wiedervereinigung Oster-
reichs mit dem Reich an der Wahl
fuer den grossdeutschen Reichstag
am 10. April 1938 sollen alle
Reichsdeutschen einschliesslich der
bisherigen österreichischen Staats-
angehörigen im Auslande in grösst-
moeglicher Zahl teilnehmen.
Es sind daher wieder Bordwahlen
auf den deutschen Schiffen vorgese-
hen. Jeder kann sein Wahlrecht
ausueben, der sich zwischen dem
1. und 15. April 1938 auf einem
deutschen Schiffe auf hoher See
befindet.
Wahlberechtigt ist jeder Reichs-
deutsche, der mindestens 20 Jahre
vollendet hat und nicht durch
ausdrückliche gesetzliche Bestim-
mung vom Wahlrecht ausgeschlossen
ist. Ausserdem muss er im Besitze
eines Stimmscheines sein. Es ist
erforderlich, sich diesen Stimmschein
unverzueglich zu verschaffen und zu
diesem Zwecke unter Vorlage von
Personalpapieren auf dem Deutschen
Generalkonsulat in Shanghai per-
sönlich vorzusprechen.
Die Durchfuehrung der Volksab-
stimmung und der Reichstagswahl
wird sich fuer alle Deutschen in
Shanghai an Bord eines deutschen
Schiffes wegen unueberwindlicher
Schwierigkeiten leider nicht ermoeg-
glichen lassen.
Stattdessen wird am 10. April 1938
ein Wahlgang stattfinden, dessen
Ergebnisse zwar nicht den amtlichen
deutschen Wahlziffern zugerechnet
werden koennen, der aber Gelegen-
heit geben soll, zu beweisen, dass
die Deutschen in aller Welt zur
Politik des Führers stehen und sich
zu der um den österreichischen
Bruderstamm erweiterten deutschen
Volksgemeinschaft bekennen.
Die Wahl findet statt
Sonntag, den 10. April 1938
in den Räumen der Deutschen
Schule am Deutschen Eck.
Nur wer einen von dem Deutschen
Generalkonsulat ausgestellten Stim-
mschein hat, ist zur Wahl zugelassen.
Zur reibungslosen Durchfuehrung
ergeht hiermit die Aufforderung,
sich moeglichst schon in den naech-
sten Tagen zur Ausstellung der
Stimmscheine zu melden. Die
grosse Anzahl der wahlberechtigten
Deutschen im Bezirke des General-
konsulats wird nur dann restlos
erfasst werden koennen, wenn der
Einzelne mit der Beschaffung des
Stimmscheines nicht bis zu den
letzten Tagen vor der Wahl wartet.
Fuer die N.S.D.A.P.—A.O.
S. LAHRMANN,
Landesgruppenleiter.
Der Leiter
des Deutschen Generalkonsulats,
M. FISCHER.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury

Anschluss Ballot
Planned In S'hai

1300 German, Austrian
Citizens To Ballot
Unofficially

Shanghai Austrians and Germans although unable to participate in the official plebiscite on the union of Germany and Austria which takes place on April 10 will nevertheless be given the opportunity of expressing their sentiments in regard to the important issue at an unofficial balloting which takes place Sunday, April 10, in the rooms of the German School on Great Western Road.

As in the past, in order to provide for the participation of as many overseas nationals as possible, overseas Germans and "former Austrians" entitled to a vote may do so if they find themselves on board a German vessel on the high seas between April 1 and 15. All Germans over the age of 20 years not disfranchised by some official decree are entitled to vote. Jews may not participate under any condition.

No ship Available

According to an announcement of Herr S. Lehrmann, leader of the National-Socialist Party in China, and Mr. M. Fischer, head of the German consulate-general, unsurmountable obstacles prevent the holding of balloting for the local community on board a vessel. The purpose of the voting at the school is therefore intended primarily to show that the Germans in this part of the world support the policy of the Fuehrer Adolf Hitler and are in favor of the anschluss. Only those with a voting permit from the German consulate-general will be permitted to participate and all are urged to make application as soon as possible. Voters are requested to avoid a last minute rush by applying early.

1500 Entitled To Vote

The local Austro-German community at present comprises approximately 1500 Germans and 100 Austrians. Of this number, 1200 Germans and 100 Austrians are believed franchised to participate in the unofficial voting.

The size of the community here is reported to prevent balloting at sea since no vessel large enough to hold all voters will be available at the time desired. Germans in other parts of China and in "Manchukuo" will also be participating in official or unofficial balloting on April 10.

BERLIN, Jan. 19.—Germans living abroad failing to enrol for military service and in the labour corps, as required under a decree issued yesterday, would not be treated as deserters when they returned to Germany later, declared official circles when questioned by Reuter to-day.

They, however, it was added, would be simply asked to do military service if they were still of military age.

If Germans abroad, it was declared, could show that they would suffer, either by their absence or other personal reasons, if they had to carry out military service, then they might be exempted.

OUR REPLY TO A LOCAL NAZI JOURNAL
GOETHE, the German poet, said, "We are never deceived; we deceive ourselves." This dictum is applicable to the Nazis who worship blindly their Chief and bow before his imperial edicts. In their sheer madness they compare him to JESUS and even greater than JESU. The New York Post publishes some typical Easter thoughts from the Nazi Press. ALOIS SPANIOL, leader of the Nazis in the Saar, declares, "Hitler is a new, and a more powerful Jesus Christ." Dr. KEHL, chairman of the Prussian Diet, exclaims: "ADOLF HITLER is the real Holy Ghost." We can cite further passages by others but let us be brief. The Nazis simply deceive themselves, according to GOETHE, and for the present it is not possible to reform them.

Our attention has been drawn to an article headed "The Dawn of anti-Semitism in China?" which was published in The Cathay Cosmopolitan, purporting to be a reply to our leader on "The German Jews and the Huguenots" which appeared in our April issue. It covers six pages with the name of the Editor of this journal mentioned over fifty times. The publication poses as a "symposium Devoted to the Advancement of International Relationships in the Far East." The reader is led to believe that it is edited by an American and registered in the name of a Briton in the British Consulate. There is nothing to show that it is a Nazi journal, supported and sponsored by the Nazis in Shanghai. In order to show that it is self-supporting it inserts advertisements of all the foreign local banks, firms and brokers, so that no one may suspect that it is not a paying concern! . . . Who will not sympathise with the exiled Germans when their country has fallen from the high position it had held in the comity of Nations?

It is but natural that the reply given us by the local Nazi publication should distort truth and resort to slander and vilification. We are charged with disregarding the label which appears in our masthead that we stand for "international goodwill among the Powers," since we criticize harshly the Nazi regime and stir up ill-feeling in consequence. Even the spirit of ISAIAH has been invoked against us, because we neglect to observe the motto lifted from Isaiah, 52-7 which adorns our front cover. We had been so inured to Nazi tactics for the past three years, that we are not a bit surprised over the subtle manner in which we are being dragged into the present controversy. We repeat again that ISRAEL'S MESSENGER is a messenger of peace and goodwill. It is not unmindful of its obligations to stand for the welfare of Asia and to bring East and West closer together. If we find ourselves impelled to criticize harshly the Nazi regime, it is because the latter has lost all sense of proportion and precipitated a terrible crisis in the civilized world. From the very outset we made it clear that our criticisms of the Nazi regime were not of our own seeking but had been thrust upon us by the cruel regime. Our quarrel is not with the German nation as a whole, but with the Government. In our issue of April last, we stated:—

"Our criticisms of Nazi perfidy in this journal, will be continued so long as the reign of terror abides in the land of Hitler. We need hardly assure the anti-Nazi Germans with whom we come into contact that we harbour no illwill against the German nation as a whole. We honour the Germany of Goethe, Heine, Kant, Schiller et. al. but abhor the Germany of Hitler, Goering, Goebbels et. al. We are doing a real service to civilization in battling against the dark forces and exposing their heinous crimes. It is hoped that our attitude will not be misunderstood. We have no desire to prolong the agony indefinitely if we can in any way help to do so. That depends upon Germany and its rulers. We would be among the first to hail the dawn of liberty in that unhappy land and support the liberators. . . ."

As to the "Original Messenger, harbinger of good tidings and happiness and a publisher of peace" and our alleged failure to live up to this motto, we can afford to laugh at the puerility shown by the Nazi critic. He who poses as a Biblical student should not forget that the same thunderer of "good tidings" also inveighed vehemently against wickedness and unrighteousness. His flaming words should burn in the ears of the leaders of the Nazi regime, which stands arraigned before the bar of public opinion. ISAIAH's denunciation is wholly applicable when he said:

But the wicked are like the troubled sea;
For it cannot rest,
And its waters cast up mire and dirt,
There is no peace,
"Saith my God concerning the wicked"—ISAIAH, 52, 20-21.

We are further taken to task for criticising Turkey, Japan and Germany in our April issue. The Nazi publication is so artful in showing its cloven hoof that it is likely to impress the unwary. It is nowhere conceded that friendly criticism of neighbours with whom one is on the best of terms is inadmissible. It certainly cannot be compared with that of the Hitler regime whose despicable treatment of Jews and others, cries to heaven for redress. If we felt impelled to remind the Japanese Embassy in London that its statement issued to the Joint Committee was not in consonance with facts that are known in Harbin and here, it was because we were convinced that it could verify them from the events that are coming to light. On three occasions misleading reports were sent to Washington regarding conditions in Harbin by officials who have axes to grind, and who are deliberately working to undermine Jewish interests and to satisfy the lust of their enemies. If we took steps to draw the attention of the Embassy to the real state of affairs, it does not imply that we had questioned the veracity of the statement made by the latter. The subtle attempt to drive a wedge will not succeed. It can be scotched with a little effort. We have no desire to waste time and space to answer in detail the petty-mindedness of the Nazi critic. Our quarrel with the Muslim Press in India is no business of the latter. In course of time, we hope to iron it out and restore our good relations which we hope will not suffer eclipse. The Semitic races are noted for their natural instincts to overcome their trouble without inviting busybodies to meddle with them. The Nazi publication can never understand the psychology advisable for the intruder to retire

我们对一份本地纳粹刊物的答复

德国诗人歌德（GOETHE）曾说：“我们从未受骗；是我们欺骗了自己。”这句格言适用于那些盲目崇拜其元首并屈从于其帝国法令的纳粹分子。他们在疯狂的极致中将他比作耶稣，甚至认为他比耶稣更伟大。《纽约邮报》刊登了一些来自纳粹报刊的典型复活节言论。萨尔地区纳粹领导人阿洛伊斯·斯帕尼奥尔（ALOIS SPANIOL）宣称：“希特勒是一位新的、更有力的耶稣基督。”普鲁士邦议会议长克尔博士（Dr. KEHL）惊呼：“阿道夫·希特勒（ADOLF HITLER）是真正的圣灵。”我们可以引用更多其他人的段落，但让我们言简意赅。根据歌德的说法，纳粹分子只是在自欺欺人，而且目前不可能改造他们。

我们注意到一篇题为《中国反犹主义的黎明？》的文章，发表在《天下月刊》（The Cathay Cosmopolitan）上，声称是对我们四月号刊登的社论《德国犹太人与胡格诺派教徒》的答复。该文长达六页，提及该刊编辑的名字五十余次。该出版物伪装成“致力于促进远东国际关系的专题讨论”。读者被引导相信它由一位美国人编辑，并以一位英国人的名义在英国领事馆注册。没有任何迹象表明它是一份由在上海的纳粹分子支持和赞助的纳粹刊物。为了显示其自负盈亏，它刊登了所有在沪外国银行、公司和经纪人的广告，以便无人怀疑它不是一家盈利机构！……当他们的国家从其在国际礼让中所占据的崇高地位跌落时，谁不会同情那些流亡的德国人呢？

本地纳粹刊物给我们的答复歪曲事实并诉诸诽谤和诋毁，这是很自然的。我们被指责无视刊头标明的立场，即我们主张“列强间的国际善意”，因为我们严厉批评纳粹政权并因此激起恶感。甚至以赛亚（ISAIAH）的精神也被用来反对我们，因为我们忽视了装饰在我们封面上的、引自《以赛亚书》52章7节的格言。在过去三年里，我们对纳粹的策略已经习以为常，因此对于被以微妙的方式拖入当前的争议，我们一点也不感到惊讶。我们要再次重申，《以色列信使报》（ISRAEL'S MESSENGER）是和平与善意的信使。它并未忘记其维护亚洲福祉以及拉近东西方距离的义务。如果我们觉得不得不严厉批评纳粹政权，那是因为后者已失去所有的分寸感，并在文明世界引发了一场可怕的危机。从一开始我们就明确表示，我们对纳粹政权的批评并非我们要自找麻烦，而是被该残酷政权强加于我们的。我们的争执对象不是整个德意志民族，而是其政府。在我们去年四月的期刊中，我们 stated：—

“只要恐怖统治还存在于希特勒的土地上，本刊对纳粹背信弃义行为的批评就将持续下去。我们几乎无需向与我们接触的反纳粹德国人保证，我们对整个德意志民族没有恶意。我们尊崇歌德、海涅、康德、席勒等人的德国，但憎恶希特勒、戈林、戈培尔等人的德国。我们在对抗黑暗势力并揭露其滔天罪行方面，正在为文明做出真正的贡献。希望我们的态度不被误解。如果我们可以以任何方式提供帮助，我们并不希望无限期地延长这种痛苦。这取决于德国及其统治者。我们将是最先欢呼那片不幸土地上的自由黎明并支持解放者的人之一。……”

至于所谓“原始的信使，好消息和幸福的先驱，和平的出版者”，以及我们未能履行这一格言的指控，我们可以一笑置之，嘲笑这位纳粹评论员所表现出的幼稚。那位自诩为圣经学者的人不应忘记，那位同样宣扬“好消息”的先知也曾猛烈抨击邪恶和不义。他那如火的话语应在纳粹政权领导人的耳中燃烧，该政权正站在舆论的审判台前受审。当以赛亚说以下话语时，他的谴责完全适用：

但恶人必如翻腾的海，
不得平静；
其中的水涌出淤泥和污秽。
“我的神说：恶人必不得平安”——《以赛亚书》52:20-21。

我们因在四月号中批评土耳其、日本和德国而进一步受到责难。这份纳粹刊物在露出其丑恶面目时如此狡猾，以至于可能会给粗心大意的人留下印象。文中从未承认，对关系最好的邻国进行友好批评是不可接受的。这当然不能与希特勒政权相提并论，后者对犹太人及其他人的卑鄙待遇，呼天抢地要求伸张正义。如果我们觉得有必要提醒驻伦敦的日本大使馆，其向联合委员会发表的声明与在哈尔滨和上海所知的事实不符，那是因为我们确信，随着事件真相大白，它可以核实这些事实。曾有三次，怀有私心且故意破坏犹太人利益以满足其敌人贪欲的官员，向华盛顿发送了关于哈尔滨局势的误导性报告。如果我们采取措施提请大使馆注意真实情况，这并不意味着我们质疑了后者声明的真实性。这种试图楔入分歧的微妙企图不会得逞。只需稍加努力即可将其挫败。我们不想浪费时间和篇幅去详细回答这位纳粹评论员的狭隘心态。我们与印度穆斯林报刊的争执与后者无关。随着时间的推移，我们希望解决这一问题并恢复我们的良好关系，希望这种关系不会蒙受阴影。闪米特种族以其不邀请好事者插手、依靠本能克服困难的特性而闻名。纳粹刊物永远无法理解那种建议入侵者退出的心理

The world has come to the conclusion that nothing would hurt the Nazi regime more than hitting back on its vulnerable spot, since all the appeals to reason have been of no avail. A sad chapter to our modern civilization has been added by the Nazi government. The torture of men, women and children, the harassing of German Jewish war veterans, crippled and disabled in military service for the Vaterland, the seizure of the savings and the property of Jews and the gradual elimination of every means of earning an honourable livelihood for Jewish men and women, the artful torture in concentration camps, the vile degeneracies . . . . . are crimes which ascend to heaven for vengeance. The Hitler regime has forfeited its right to be reckoned as a civilized Power and has placed itself beyond the pale of civilization. Although the Nations are obliged to carry on conversations with her, it is because for the present there is no way out. Sir NORMAN ANGELL, at the annual general meeting of the World Non-Sectarian anti-Nazi Council to Champion Human Rights, held in London in April last, was outspoken in his denunciation of the Hitler regime. Said he:—

"Heaven knew that they had no feeling against the German people. But if a friend suddenly got into his head to burn down one's house because he did not like its architecture, to destroy one's home and debauch one's children, were they going to continue to play golf with him as though nothing had happened, and were they going to organize the Olympic Games with him?"

Thus spoke one of England's great champions for human rights, whose words must burn in the ears of every Nazi on earth. We are confident that such outspokenness will win many a recalcitrant foe for suffering humanity and impel the world to reflect on what is being done to rob the latter of its hard-earned rights. We fight to-day for "dumb" human beings who cannot speak for themselves. The local Nazi journal has, to our surprise, suddenly developed a taste to protect Jewish interests in China! It broods over the prospects of a wave of anti-Semitism being let loose on China's soil and warns us that if we do not suppress our legitimate criticism of the Hitler regime, we would be responsible for creating an embarrassing position for the Jews out here! This clever ruse is characteristic of the Nazis. We can afford to spurn the threat. Our readers have commended us for defending the rights of the oppressed and the suppressed in Nazi Germany. Our Chinese neighbours who read this journal carefully, understand well the role we are playing and consequently have not hesitated in expressing commiseration.

The attack on us has been wound up by making a feeble and clumsy attempt to belittle the facts and figures given in our April issue, regarding the role played by German Jews in the Great War and the actual sacrifices made by them. The Nazi publication clothes itself in the mantle of a saint in trying to whitewash the guilt of its government in its barbaric treatment of the Jews, by ignoring the figures cited by us from reliable and authentic sources. This is nothing novel. All the way through the Nazis have behaved shamelessly. Soon after the war Dietrich Eckart, editor of an anti-Semitic Munich weekly, offered a prize of 1,000 marks to anybody who could prove that there was even one Jewish family that had had three sons in the trenches for three weeks. Thereupon, a Rabbi of Hanover furnished a list of twenty Jewish families in his community that fulfilled this condition, and a further list of fifty Jewish families from other communities which had had seven or eight sons in the field, and some of which had had to mourn the loss of three sons. HERMANN BRANDAT, noted Christian-German author, playwright and poet, in an illuminating article on the "Crisis in Germany," repudiates the many fallacious concepts that have been deliberately fostered by the Nazi regime as a justification of its own nefarious policy. Commenting on Jewish contributions the eminent author says:—

"The Jews in Germany did their duty in the war just as every other German. Twelve and a half percent. of them died for the Fatherland, whereas the corresponding ratio of all other Germans was thirteen and a half. Thirty-five thousand received Orders for bravery, twenty-three thousand were promoted to non-commissioned positions, and two thousand became officers. And before the World War, no Jew was permitted to attain to an officer's position! One hundred and sixty-five Jews were aviators at the front, thirty of whom fell in battle."

With unabashed impudence the local Nazi publication seeks to disparage the above and cites Government figures to support its shameless propaganda in China! This is characteristic of the Nazis. It bears out the injunction laid down in Hitler's "Bible" "My Struggle," German edition, page 200:

"The task of propaganda is not the consideration of diverse rights. Its objective is not to seek out the truth, insofar as it may be favourable to the other side. But (propaganda) must ceaselessly serve its own ends."

Germany's degradation as a moral force is now an unchallengeable fact, and if one were a Nazi and conscious of his Government's apostasy, he would hide himself in holes and no longer boast of his pernicious cult. Medievalism is not an answer to our modern culture, and it is not amazing that the enlightened German elements are awakening to the danger into which their name and fame have been dragged by an immoral regime. Rev. WALTER CARL SUBKE, Pastor of Greenwich Presbyterian Church, New York, spoke candidly and fearlessly in his sermon during the last Armistice Day on "Hitlerism: Hub of Hate," when he said:—

"It is high time that public opinion, as the greatest court of the world, should convene and take its aroused passion for God and humanity firmly in the hands with the determination to drive Hitlerism out of the sacred temple of humanity."

Public opinion is a second conscience. The foolish and the dead alone never change their opinion. The German Pastor in his rousing message to his countrymen will yet awaken the decency and right-mindedness of all true German patriots.

我们的纳粹批评者哀叹我们呼吁读者抵制德国商品和服务。或许必须指出，在整个文明世界，对德国的经济抵制正在被严格执行。国际法承认使用经济制裁作为对付共同敌人的和平武器。在许多出版物中，我们可以看到提醒人们不要“购买任何德国制造的东西”。世界已得出结论，既然所有理性的呼吁都无济于事，那么打击其薄弱环节是对纳粹政权最大的伤害。纳粹政府为我们现代文明增添了一个悲惨的篇章。对男女儿童的折磨，对为祖國（Vaterland）服役致残的德国犹太退伍军人的骚扰，没收犹太人的储蓄和财产，并逐步消除犹太男女获得体面生计的一切手段，集中营里巧妙的酷刑，卑鄙的堕落……这些都是罪大恶极、天理难容的罪行。希特勒政权已丧失了被视为文明国家的权利，并将自己置于文明之外。虽然各国不得不与其进行对话，但这只是因为目前别无他法。诺曼·安吉尔爵士（Sir NORMAN ANGELL）在去年四月于伦敦举行的世界非宗派反纳粹人权捍卫委员会年度大会上，直言不讳地谴责了希特勒政权。他说：—

“天知道我们对德国人民并无恶感。但是，如果一个朋友突然因为不喜欢某人的房屋建筑风格而决定烧毁它，摧毁某人的家园并腐蚀其子女，他们是否还要像什么都没发生一样继续和他打高尔夫球，是否还要和他一起组织奥林匹克运动会？”

这位英国伟大的人权捍卫者如是说，他的话语必定让世上每一个纳粹分子感到如芒在背。我们相信，这种坦率将为受苦的人类赢得许多顽固的敌人，并促使世界反思正在发生的剥夺人类来之不易的权利的行为。我们今天为那些无法为自己发声的“沉默”人类而战。令我们惊讶的是，当地的纳粹刊物突然表现出保护在华犹太人利益的姿态！它担忧反犹主义浪潮在中国土地上爆发，并警告我们，如果我们不抑制对希特勒政权的正当批评，我们将对造成此地犹太人的尴尬处境负责！这种狡猾的伎俩是纳粹的典型特征。我们可以不屑于这种威胁。我们的读者称赞我们捍卫了纳粹德国受压迫和被压制者的权利。仔细阅读本刊物的中国邻居们很好地理解了我们所扮演的角色，因此毫不犹豫地表达了同情。

对我们的攻击最终以一种软弱且笨拙的方式结束，试图贬低我们四月刊中关于德国犹太人在大战中所起作用及实际牺牲的事实和数据。该纳粹出版物试图通过无视我们引用的可靠且真实来源的数据，披上圣人的外衣，为其政府在对待犹太人方面的野蛮行径洗白罪责。这并不新鲜。纳粹一直表现得厚颜无耻。战后不久，慕尼黑一家反犹周刊的编辑迪特里希·埃卡特（Dietrich Eckart）悬赏1000马克，奖励任何能证明哪怕有一个犹太家庭有三个儿子在战壕里待满三周的人。随后，汉诺威的一位拉比提供了一份名单，列出了他所在社区中符合这一条件的二十个犹太家庭，以及来自其他社区的五十个犹太家庭的进一步名单，这些家庭有七到八个儿子在前线，其中一些家庭不得不哀悼失去三个儿子的悲痛。赫尔曼·布兰达特（HERMANN BRANDAT），著名的基督教德国作家、剧作家和诗人，在一篇关于“德国危机”的发人深省的文章中，驳斥了纳粹政权为证明其邪恶政策正当性而故意培育的许多谬误概念。在评论犹太人的贡献时，这位著名作者说：—

“德国犹太人在战争中尽了自己的责任，就像其他每个德国人一样。他们中有百分之十二点五为祖国而死，而其他所有德国人的相应比例为百分之十三点五。三万五千人获得了英勇勋章，两万三千人晋升为士官，两千人成为军官。而在世界大战之前，没有任何犹太人被允许担任军官职位！一百六十五名犹太人是前线的飞行员，其中三十人在战斗中阵亡。”

当地纳粹刊物厚颜无耻地试图贬低上述内容，并引用政府数据来支持其在中国的无耻宣传！这是纳粹的典型特征。这印证了希特勒“圣经”《我的奋斗》德文版第200页规定的训诫：

“宣传的任务不是考虑各种权利。其目标不是寻求真理，只要这对另一方有利。但（宣传）必须不断地服务于其自身目的。”

德国作为道德力量的堕落现在是一个无可争议的事实，如果一个人是纳粹分子并意识到其政府的背叛，他会躲进洞里，不再吹嘘其有害的邪教。中世纪主义不是对我们现代文化的答案，开明的德国人士正觉醒到他们的名声被一个不道德的政权拖入的危险之中，这并不令人惊讶。纽约格林威治长老会教堂牧师沃尔特·卡尔·苏布克牧师（Rev. WALTER CARL SUBKE）在去年停战日的布道中，就“希特勒主义：仇恨的核心”坦诚而无畏地发言，他说：—

“是时候让作为世界最高法庭的公众舆论召开会议，将其对上帝和人类的激昂热情 firmly 掌握在手中，决心将希特勒主义从人类的神圣殿堂中驱逐出去。”

公众舆论是第二良知。只有愚者和死者才从不改变观点。这位德国牧师在向同胞发出的鼓舞人心的信息中，终将唤醒所有真正德国爱国者的正派和正直思想。

spring weather. Many German busi-

In the invitation circulated
among local Nazis, native costumes
representing different parts of Ger-

started after dark, proceeded by a
general get-together on the lawn

德国人在此开设纳粹党俱乐部

大批人群聚集于点岛举行仪式

昨天下午，大批当地德国人参加了位于吴淞附近点岛的纳粹俱乐部会所的开幕式。新组织以帝国总统希特勒的口号“力量来自欢乐”（Kraft Durch Freude）命名，将成为此地纳粹分子的度假胜地。
昨天为从上海前往的成员提供了专用汽车和巴士。随着温暖的春日天气，许多德国商人及其家属聚集在威廉皇帝学校等待交通工具。
在当地纳粹分子中流传的邀请函中，要求参加派对时穿着代表德国不同地区的民族服装。
庆祝活动的正式部分在天黑后开始，此前在俱乐部住所的草坪上进行了普遍的聚会。
点岛由沙沉积物组成。这块土地归中国政府所有，作为度假胜地出租给各个团体。

Memorandum on the Affairs of the Local Nazi Party

A branch of the "Nationalsozialistische Deutsche
Arbeiterpartei" or, as it is better known, the "Nazi Party",
has been in existence in Shanghai since 1929. It has
branches in Canton, Hongkong, Manila, Nanking, Tsinanfu,
Tsingtae, Tientsin, Harbin, Mukden, Osaka and Kobe. The
aims of the Nazi Party in Shanghai and other parts of the
Far East are :-

1. To teach and instruct German citizens in the tenets
and beliefs of Nationalism-Socialism, and to explain
to them the methods whereby Hitler will enable Germany
to recover her position as one of the Great Nations
of the World.

2. To instil patriotic fervour into the minds of German
citizens with the ultimate object of raising the
Third Reich into an all-powerful and national State.

3. To teach German citizens to refrain from meddling in the
politics and affairs of countries in which they reside.
For example, Germans in the Far East are forbidden to
participate in the official activities of Chinese,
White Russians, Koreans and Japanese, etc.

4. To teach Germans to become "open-minded" and not to
become involved in any secret movements.

The local followers of Hitler appear to hold a belief
that it is impossible for German Jews to adapt themselves
to their line of political thought so they have been
deliberately excluded from those German circles which the
Nazis are trying to influence. The general trend of
opinion among local elder Nazis is definitely not of an
anti-Semitic nature.

The members of the Nazi Party in Shanghai are carefully
selected. No person is considered eligible for membership

关于当地纳粹党事务的备忘录

“国家社会主义德国工人党”（Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei），或更广为人知的“纳粹党”，自1929年以来在上海设有分支。它在广州、香港、马尼拉、南京、济南府、青岛、天津、哈尔滨、沈阳、大阪和神户设有分支机构。纳粹党在上海及远东其他地区的目标是：-

1. 向德国公民传授和教导民族社会主义的原则和信仰，并向他们解释希特勒将使德国恢复其作为世界大国之一地位的方法。

2. 向德国公民灌输爱国热情，最终目的是将第三 Reich 提升为一个全能的国家状态。

3. 教导德国公民避免干涉其居住国的政治和事务。例如，禁止远东的德国人参与中国人、白俄人、朝鲜人和日本人等的官方活动。

希特勒的当地追随者似乎认为，德国犹太人不可能适应他们的政治思想路线，因此他们被刻意排除在纳粹试图影响的德国圈子之外。当地资深纳粹分子的普遍舆论倾向 definitely 不具有反犹性质。

Important Press
Correction

In the "North-China Daily News"
of March 31 the account of the
German Election contained a para-
graph from a despatch by a Berlin
correspondent of the United Press
Associations as transmitted to this
office by the Shanghai Branch of
the Agency. This paragraph stated
that "burglars had entered the
offices of the Ministry of Pro-
paganda and stolen the tabulated
results of the Election, which had
presumably been compiled weeks in
advance." The message was received
and published in good faith; but,
owing to information received
the next day from the German Con-
sul-General, specific inquiries were
made of the United Press Associa-
tions together with an urgent re-
quest for telegraphic verification.
As the result of these inquiries the
following message has been received
from the Shanghai office of the
United Press Associations:

With reference to our Berlin
despatch of March 29 (Sheet 6 of
March 30 Service) regarding the
German Election, our New York
office advises us that the second
paragraph should have read as
follows:

Berliners this afternoon con-
tinued to flock to the polls,
apparently heedless of the hoary
joke, resurrected for the cam-
paign, that burglars had broken
into the Ministry of Propaganda
last week and stolen the Election
results.

Covering this message a letter,
dated April 1, from Mr. John R.
Morris, Far Eastern manager of the
United Press Associations, was also
received in the following terms:

We beg to call your attention to
the correction we have issued
to-day of a March 29th despatch
from Berlin. The correction will
make it clear that the correspondent
writing the despatch in Berlin had
no intention of insinuating that
results of the Sunday election in
Germany had been prepared in
advance, but was merely making
casual reference to a joke to this
effect which had been circulated
there. That the despatch as
received here gave an erroneous
impression appears to have been the
result of mutilation or misinter-
pretation of the original despatch
in the course of transmission be-
tween Berlin and Shanghai.
We regret exceedingly the incon-
venience the "North-China Daily
News" has suffered as result of
publishing the erroneous version
received here.

In publishing the correction to
this unfortunate mistake, for which

重要更正

在3月31日的《字林西报》中，关于德国选举的报道包含了一段由合众通讯社（United Press Associations）柏林记者发回、并经该社上海分社转至本报的电讯稿。该段文字称：“窃贼闯入宣传部办公室，偷走了据信已在数周前编制好的选举统计结果。”该消息系出于善意接收并刊登；但由于次日从德国总领事处获得信息，本报随即向合众通讯社进行具体查询，并紧急请求电报核实。经此查询，收到合众通讯社上海办事处发来的如下消息：

关于我们3月29日发自柏林的电讯稿（3月30日服务第6页）涉及德国选举一事，我社纽约办事处告知，第二段原文应为：

“柏林市民今天下午继续涌向投票站，显然对那个为竞选而重新翻出的陈腐笑话毫不在意——该笑话称窃贼上周闯入了宣传部，偷走了选举结果。”

随附此消息的还有合众通讯社远东经理约翰·R·莫里斯（John R. Morris）先生4月1日来信，内容如下：

谨提请贵报注意，我社今日已就3月29日发自柏林的电讯稿发出更正。此次更正将表明，在柏林撰写该电讯稿的记者无意暗示德国周日选举的结果是预先准备好的，而只是随意提及当地流传的一个此类笑话。该电讯稿在此间收悉时给人造成错误印象，似乎是由于原稿在从柏林传输至上海的过程中遭到删改或误译所致。
对于《字林西报》因刊登此处收到的错误版本而遭受的不便，我们深表歉意。

本刊在刊登这一不幸错误的更正时（该错误由通讯社承担责任），愿与对德籍读者表示歉意之意保持一致，因为原始消息给这些读者带来了极大的痛苦。

REICH SOLIDLY BEHIND
ITS FÜHRER

Overwhelming Endorsement of Herr Adolf Hitler's
Foreign Policies

98.79 PER CENT. MAJORITY RECORDED

Heaviest Vote in History: Outcome of Referendum
Never in Doubt

VOTERS of the Reich yesterday gave their overwhelming en-
dorsement to the action of the Reichsfuehrer, Herr Adolf
Hitler, in denouncing the Versailles and Locarno treaties and
undertaking the military re-occupation of the Rhineland.
The outcome of the referendum was never in doubt, says
United Press from Berlin. Actually, the results were known long
before the people went to the polls, inasmuch as burglars last week
entered the offices of the Ministry of Propaganda and stole the
tabulated results of the election which had presumably been com-
piled weeks in advance.
Nevertheless, the real vote was the heaviest in history. The
majority given to the policies of Herr Hitler exceeded 98 per cent.,
and the result, in effect, was Herr Hitler's answer to the other
signatories of the Locarno Pact: the overwhelming support indicated
beyond a doubt that Germany is ready to back the Führer in
peace or war.

OSTASIATISCHER LLOYD
Mittwoch, den 1. April, 1936
13945

Fuer den Hausgebrauch der
"North-China Daily News".

Die "North-China Daily News" hat es fuer noetig befunden, in ihrer gestrigen Ausgabe in einer Zusammenstellung der Nachrichten ueber den deutschen Wahlausgang mit besonderer Hervorhebung die folgenden Zeilen zu schreiben:
"The outcome of the referendum was never in doubt, says United Press from Berlin. Actually, the results were known long before the people went to the polls, inasmuch as burglars last week entered the offices of the Ministry of Propaganda and stole the tabulated results of the election, which had presumably been compiled weeks in advance."
Sofort nach Bekanntwerden dieser Meldung haben das Deutsche Generalkonsulat, die Landesleitung der N.S.D.A.P., die Deutsche Gemeinde und die Deutsche Handelskammer an den Hauptschriftleiter der Zeitung ein Schreiben des Inhalts gesandt, dass diese Ausfuehrungen in der deutschen Gemeinde Schanghais die schaerfste Empoerung hervorgerufen haetten. Man erwarte von der "North-China Daily News" eine sofortige Klarstellung der Angelegenheit; andernfalls wuerde man sich zu weiteren Schritten veranlasst sehen.
Das Schreiben des Deutschen Generalkonsulats befristete die Antwort auf fuenf Uhr nachmittags. Der Hauptschriftleiter der "North-China Daily News" hat es daraufhin fuer richtig gehalten, in einer Form zu antworten, die als taktlos empfunden werden musste und zum mindesten verriet, dass ihr Absender, der Chefredakteur dieses Blattes, nicht im Geringsten verstanden hatte, welche Beweggruende dem deutschen Protest zugrundelagen.
Daraufhin wurde seitens des Deutschen Generalkonsulats ein nochmaliges Schreiben gesandt, in dem, ebenfalls bis zu einer spaeteren Stunde befristet, eine Antwort darauf verlangt wurde, ob die "North-China Daily News" bereit sei, in ihrer naechsterreichbaren Ausgabe eine Richtigstellung und eine Klarstellung der Angelegenheit zu bringen. Die Antwort, die dem Deutschen Generalkonsulat zuteil wurde, ging und in der auch der Chefredakteur der Zeitung bereit erklaerte, eine von dem Konsulat einzusendende Richtigstellung zu bringen, sofern diese unparteiisch abgefasst sei, muss als eine grobe Unverschaeumtheit bezeichnet werden, und hat selbstverstaendlich keinerlei Entgegnung mehr gefunden.
Wir duerfen den Fall unsererseits zunaechst von der journalistischen Seite her betrachten. Der redaktionelle Leiter dieses Blattes, der sich Chefredakteur nennt, hat also von dem Handwerkszeug im Journalismus so wenig Ahnung, dass er sich in seinem Schreiben an das Deutsche Generalkonsulat damit "verteidigt", die "North-China Daily News" habe diese Aeusserungen lediglich im Rahmen eines Telegramms, das von der United Press bearbeitet wurde, gebracht und sei deshalb fuer den Inhalt dieser Meldung nicht verantwortlich zu machen.
Jeder Schriftleiter der kleinsten Provinzzeitung aber weiss, dass die von den Nachrichtenagenturen gelieferten Meldungen lediglich das Rohmaterial fuer die Zeitung bilden. An der Verarbeitung und Verwendung dieses Stoffes erkennt man die journalistische Durchbildung eines Schriftleiters und im Besonderen auch seine Begabung und sein Taktgefuehl.
Ein Schriftleiter, der diese notwendigsten Voraussetzungen fuer seinen Beruf nicht mitbringt, taugt fuer seinen Posten nicht und wird zu einem hoeheren Posten nur dann aufsteigen, wenn der Verlag an das Niveau seines Blattes keine besonderen Anforderungen stellt. Wir wissen nicht, welche Anforderungen der Verlag der "North-China Daily News" an die redaktionelle Gestaltung seines Blattes stellt; das ist schliesslich und zunaechst auch eine Angelegenheit im Hause selbst.
Wenn die Leistungen der Schriftleitung sich aber in einer Form wie der vorliegenden fuer den Leserkreis wahrnehmbar aeussern, dann hat sich darum auch der Leser- und Inserentenkreis dieser Zeitung zu kuemmern. Das wird die deutsche Kolonie, wie in der gestrigen Generalversammlung der Deutschen Gemeinde selbst fuer einen wenig qualifizierten Redakteur unschwer zu erkennen gewesen waere, mit besonderer Gruendlichkeit tun.
Wenn die "North-China Daily News" sich die Muehe machen wollte, in ihrer Ausgabe vom Montag nachzulesen, dann koennte sie dort feststellen, dass der vergangene Sonntag auch einen deutschen Wahltag in Schanghai brachte, und dass das Ergebnis dieser Wahl eine geschlossene deutsche politische Front zeigte.
Diese politische deutsche Front in Schanghai erklaert der "North-China Daily News", dass sie die Diffamierungen und bewussten Falschmeldungen dieses Blattes mit aller Entschiedenheit zurueckweist. Die Zeiten, in denen ein auslaendisches Blatt glaubte, ihre eigenen Leser mit bewussten Falschmeldungen ueber deutsches Geschehen versehen zu koennen, sind endgueltig vorbei. Die deutschen Interessen sind heute so gross wie die jeder anderen Nation, und es ist daher nicht einzusehen, warum die deutsche Kolonie in Schanghai sich derartige Journalisten leisten soll, die den Standpunkt der deutschen Kreise mit einem recht fragwuerdigen Ehrgeiz und wenig Sachkenntnis wieder zurueck zu bekommen.
Hat man auf diesem internationalen Boden in Schanghai an die grosse deutsche Gemeinde nur zu oft verschiedene, und wie man meint, berechtigte Wuensche, dann sollte man sich bestrebt sein, die Erfuellung dieser Wuensche nicht durch wuerdeloses Benehmen selbst zu unterbinden. Der Chefredakteur der "North-China Daily News" darf fuer seine sogenannte Politik aber den Erfolg verbuchen, dass die deutsche Kolonie weniger als je geneigt sein wird, derartigen Wuenschen ihr Gehoer zu schenken.
Es scheint so, dass neben die Begriffe von Ehrgefuehl und Respektierung dieses Gefuehls bei anderen doch auch eine recht gewoehnliche Ansicht besteht. Die deutsche Gemeinde wird es sich angelegen sein lassen, in Zukunft nur noch mit denjenigen Verkehr zu pflegen, die ihre Gefuehle, im besonderen ihre nationalen Gefuehle, auf das Peinlichste respektieren.

《字林西报》认为有必要在其昨日的版面中，在汇编有关德国选举结果的新闻时，特别突出地刊登了以下几行文字：
“合众通讯社自柏林报道，公投结果从未存疑。实际上，早在民众前往投票站之前，结果便已为人所知，因为窃贼上周闯入了宣传部办公室，偷走了据信已在数周前编制好的选举统计结果。”
此消息一经传出，德国总领事馆、纳粹党地区领导层、德国侨民会和德国商会立即联名致信该报主编，指出这些言论在上海德国侨民中引起了最强烈的愤慨。人们要求《字林西报》立即澄清此事；否则将被迫采取进一步措施。
德国总领事馆的信函将回复期限定为下午五时。《字林西报》主编随后认为以某种形式回复是恰当的，但这种回复方式必然被视为失礼，且至少暴露出该报主编完全未能理解德国抗议背后的动机。
鉴于此，德国总领事馆再次去信，同样设定了较晚的截止时间，要求答复《字林西报》是否愿意在其下一期可发行的版面中刊登更正并澄清此事。德国总领事馆收到的回复中，该报主编甚至表示，只要更正内容公正无私，愿意刊登由领事馆提交的更正声明，这种回复可谓粗鲁无礼，自然未再得到任何回应。
我们可以先从新闻业务的角度来看待此事。该报自称主编的编辑负责人，对新闻工作的技巧知之甚少，以至于他在致德国总领事馆的信中以《字林西报》仅是刊登了由合众通讯社处理过的电讯稿为由进行“辩护”，因此不对该消息的内容负责。
然而，即使是最小的省级报纸的编辑也知道，通讯社提供的消息仅仅是报纸的原材料。对这些材料的加工和使用，体现了一名编辑的新闻素养，特别是其天赋和分寸感。
一名不具备这些职业最基本前提条件的编辑，是不胜任其职位的；只有当出版方对其报刊的水平没有特殊要求时，他才可能晋升到更高的职位。我们不知道《字林西报》出版方对其报刊的编辑编排有何要求；这终究首先也是其内部事务。
但是，如果编辑部的表现以如此形式呈现给读者群，那么该报的读者和广告客户群体就有必要对此予以关注。正如在德国侨民会昨天的全体大会上，即便是一个不太合格的编辑也容易被识别出来一样，德国侨民界将以特别的彻底性来处理此事。
如果《字林西报》愿意费心查阅其周一的版面，就会发现，过去的周日也是上海的一个德国选举日，且这次选举的结果显示了一个团结一致的德国政治阵线。
上海的这个德国政治阵线向《字林西报》声明，坚决拒绝该报的诽谤和故意虚假报道。外国报纸认为可以用故意的虚假报道向其读者提供有关德国事件信息的时代已经彻底结束。德国的利益如今与其他任何国家一样重大，因此无法理解为何上海德国侨民界要容忍那些以可疑的野心和浅薄的专业知识来歪曲德国各界立场的记者。
在上海这片国际土地上，人们对庞大的德国侨民社区往往有许多不同且被认为是合理的要求，那么人们应努力避免通过无礼的行为自行阻碍这些要求的实现。《字林西报》主编可以为其所谓的政策记上一功，那就是德国侨民界比以往任何时候都更不愿意倾听此类要求。
看来，除了荣誉感和尊重他人这种情感的概念外，还存在一种相当普通的观点。德国侨民界将致力于今后只与那些极其尊重其情感、特别是其民族情感的人士交往。

Subject Anti-Semite Propaganda

Made by Cler. Asst. Cook Forwarded by Gilmore Acd

JEWS IN GERMANY
Mr. Fuerholzer's Lecture

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—In your to-day's issue you publish extracts from an address given by Mr. Edmond Fuerholzer before the American Association of University Women at the American school yesterday on "Germany and Central Europe."
Referring to the "Jewish people," Mr. Fuerholzer tells us there are "two causes" which stand against them. First:
..........the large and ever-growing population of Jews in Germany which naturally tended to decrease the opportunities for economic and scientific recognition for the German people because so many places of importance in these lines were held by Jews.
What a compliment the last sentence conveys to the latter, they who lived over one thousand years in Germany and contributed much of their skill and talents for its progress and advancement! However let that pass. Exception to the line of reasoning of Mr. Fuerholzer may be taken on the ground that according to the German Immigration Department statistics 311,699 aliens passed through German seaports during the years 1919 to 1931. Of these three hundred thousand odd immigrants only 11,299 stayed for any considerable period in Germany. During the War the German Supreme Command, Gen. Ludendorff, ordered Polish and Lithuanian Jews to work in German mines or as unskilled labourers. Some of them remained after the War. Some Jews from Russia, Poland and the Ukraine came to Germany flying before Bolshevism and pogroms. But in spite of all, the total number of Jews (German and foreign) residing in Germany decreased, from 1910 to 1925, from 615,021 to 564,379 (according to the official census). In 1925, 99,000 foreign Jews resided in Germany; since then, on account of the economic crisis, thousands of them have emigrated to France, South America, Palestine and also back to Poland. In 1933 there were, in fact, not more than 76,000 East European Jews in Germany compared with nearly 65 million inhabitants.
It is hoped that your readers will notice the facts cited above as against the allegations of Mr. Fuerholzer and judge for themselves how far he was justified in seeking to propagandize the Nazi régime before a cultured audience.
The second point adduced by the speaker goes on to show "the large influx of Jewish refugees from the Soviet revolutions in Poland and Russia who, when the revolution came in Germany, fought for Communism." One cannot stand for long on a crippled leg. His fall is sure to follow very soon. Too much capital has been made out for the Hitler régime and the plea that it "stands to-day as the greatest bulwark in Europe against Communism" is discredited in serious circles. The Communist vote in Germany never exceeded 6 millions among over 40 million voters. The Communists never returned more than 100 members to Parliament among about 600. The majority of the Communist voters were not staunch Communists, but rather people who wanted to protest against their distress. The membership of the Communist party never exceeded 200,000 and not all of them would have been prepared to fight against the well-equipped Reichswehr, the police forces and the Stahlhelm. One should not forget the Communists had no influence at all in the trade unions. Every strike they attempted against the will of the trade unions was a decisive failure. Surely Hitler was not necessary to save Germany and the world from an imaginary Communist danger. But the Nazi Government, although officially hostile to Communism, was not averse to using their methods. Here is a passage from the book of Prof. Calvin B. Hoover, "Germany enters the Third Reich":
During the latter part of February the writer had revisited Soviet Russia after an absence of some three years. In Russia there was famine, an increased terror and the failure to recognize the economic expectations of the spring of 1930. The writer had returned to Germany with the feeling that if the National Socialist régime was the alternative to Bolshevism, then much could be forgiven it. If a curtailment of individual liberty under a dictatorship were the price which had to be paid to avoid the unlimited terror which held sway in Russia, then the price seemed worth paying. The writer was astonished to discover that the conditions of terror in Russia were being rapidly duplicated in Germany.
I may or may not succeed in "converting" Mr. Fuerholzer to see his own Government from another angle, but I shall be satisfied if your readers would accept his allegations not with a grain of salt but with a bucket of salt.
MENTOR.
Shanghai, Jan. 14.

Fuerholzer 先生的演讲

致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——在今日的报纸上，贵刊刊登了 Edmond Fuerholzer 先生昨日在美国学校向美国大学妇女协会发表的关于“德国与中欧”演讲的摘录。
在提及“犹太民族”时，Fuerholzer 先生告诉我们，有“两个原因”不利于他们。第一：
..........德国庞大且不断增长的犹太人口，这自然倾向于减少德国人在经济和科学领域获得认可的机会，因为这些领域的重要职位多由犹太人占据。
最后一句话对后者真是莫大的恭维，他们在德国生活了一千多年，并为德国的进步和发展贡献了大量的技能与才华！不过暂且不论。我们可以基于以下理由对 Fuerholzer 先生的推论提出异议：根据德国移民局统计，1919年至1931年间，共有311,699名外国人通过德国海港。在这三十多万移民中，只有11,299人在德国停留了较长时间。战争期间，德军最高统帅部鲁登道夫将军命令波兰和立陶宛犹太人在德国矿山工作或担任非技术劳工。其中一些人在战后留了下来。一些来自俄罗斯、波兰和乌克兰的犹太人为逃避布尔什维克主义和大屠杀来到德国。但尽管如此，居住在德国的犹太人总数（包括德国籍和外籍）从1910年的615,021人减少到1925年的564,379人（根据官方人口普查）。1925年，有99,000名外籍犹太人居住在德国；此后，由于经济危机，其中数千人移民至法国、南美洲、巴勒斯坦，也有返回波兰的。事实上，1933年德国的东欧犹太人不超过76,000人，而当时总人口近6,500万。
希望读者注意到上述事实，以反驳 Fuerholzer 先生的指控，并自行判断他在受过教育的受众面前宣扬纳粹政权的行为有多少正当性。
演讲者提出的第二点旨在显示“来自波兰和俄罗斯苏维埃革命的大量犹太难民涌入，当德国发生革命时，他们为共产主义而战。”跛足难久立。他的垮台必将很快随之而来。希特勒政权借此大做文章，声称其“如今是欧洲对抗共产主义的最大堡垒”，这一说法在严肃圈子里已失去信誉。在德国超过4,000万选民中，共产党得票数从未超过600万。在约600个议会席位中，共产党人从未获得超过100个席位。大多数共产党选民并非坚定的共产主义者，而是想要抗议自身困境的人。共产党员人数从未超过20万，而且并非所有人都准备与装备精良的国防军、警察部队和钢盔团作战。人们不应忘记，共产党在工会中毫无影响力。他们违背工会意愿试图发动的每一次罢工都以彻底失败告终。诚然，拯救德国和世界免受想象中的共产主义危险并不需要希特勒。但是，纳粹政府虽然官方上敌视共产主义，却不介意使用共产主义者的方法。以下是 Calvin B. Hoover 教授所著《德国进入第三帝国》一书中的一段话：
二月下旬，作者在阔别约三年后重访苏维埃俄罗斯。在俄罗斯，存在饥荒、恐怖加剧以及未能实现1930年春季的经济预期等情况。作者回到德国时感到，如果国家社会主义政权是布尔什维克主义的替代方案，那么它可以被宽恕许多。如果独裁统治下个人自由的缩减是为避免俄罗斯盛行的无限恐怖所必须付出的代价，那么这个代价似乎是值得的。作者惊讶地发现，俄罗斯的恐怖状况正在德国迅速重演。
我或许能成功，或许不能成功“转化”Fuerholzer 先生，让他从另一个角度看待自己的政府，但如果贵刊读者对他的指控不是持怀疑态度，而是极度怀疑，我就心满意足了。
MENTOR。
上海，1月14日。

At Frankfurt Meet

(Transocean-Kuo Min)
FRANKFURT, Feb. 15.—Within the program of winter-relief arrangements organized by the China Institute here, Herr Hasenoehrl, head of the foreign department of the Reichs Ministry of Propaganda, delivered a lecture at Frankfurt University on “Germans in China.”
The speaker described in what esteem the Germans in the Far East had been held before the war in spite of their small number and how they had succeeded in regaining the high respect, in which they were formerly held.
The mission of these Germans, said the lecturer, is not only of an economic nature, they also carry out the task of increasing the understanding for the Far East in Germany and vice versa for Germany in the Far East. China, in some respects, is going through a similar evolution as Germany and is likewise struggling to obtain recognition of her equal rights.
The address was received with much applause by the distinguished audience, the President of the China Institute, Dr. Russell, expressing hearty thanks for the instructive lecture.

COPY OF REPORT DATED JULY 19,1934.
ON POLITICAL CONDITIONS IN LOCAL GERMAN COMMUNITY.
----------------------------------------------------

Since the time of Hitler's coming into power, the local
German community has been divided into two groups: a group
consiting of persons who have accepted the new regime, but
were still impregnate with the ideas of the past, and a group
composed of 100% partisans of the new regime.

The former group, which may be referred to as "the ancients",
consists mainly of the moderate and influential elements of
the local German community including German business men.

The opposing group is composed of the local branch of
the German National Socialist Party and also includes all
extremist elements, such as: representatives of the younger
generation, and majority of members of the Storm Troops
("Sturm Abteilungen").

It was the latter group, which, in the beginning of 1934,
led a furious struggle against "the ancients" in order to take
control not only of the political life of the German community,
but also in order to meddle with questions of social and economic
order, presenting interest for Germany or Germans.

The struggle became more pronounced recently, after Mr.
Hannig had taken over the leadership of the local branch of
the German National Socialist Party. By his ultra-nationalist
and radical attitude this individual has already created many
conflicts amongst members of the community.

Mr. Hasencohrl, Commissary of the German National
Socialist Party in the Far East, who arrived in Shanghai on
May 6, 1934, endeavoured to reconcile the views of the
two parties, but was not successful in this as he did not
possess the necessary authority.

As a result of Mr. Hasencohrl's failure the strifes
became more intense. Mr. Hasencohrl gradually fell under the
influence of the extremists, following which he encountered a
pages.zh:
1934年7月19日报告副本。
关于当地德国社区的政治状况。
----------------------------------------------------

自希特勒掌权以来，当地德国社区分裂为两个群体：一个群体由接受新政权但仍深受过去思想影响的人组成；另一个群体则由新政权100%的支持者组成。

前者可称为“老派”，主要由当地德国社区中温和且有影响力的成员组成，包括德国商人。

对立群体由德国国家社会主义党当地分部组成，也包括所有极端分子，例如：年轻一代的代表，以及冲锋队（“Sturm Abteilungen”）的大多数成员。

正是后者在1934年初发起了一场激烈的斗争，以反对“老派”，目的不仅是为了掌控德国社区的政治生活，也是为了干涉涉及德国或德国人利益的社会和经济秩序问题。

自从汉尼格（Hannig）先生接管德国国家社会主义党当地分部的领导权后，这种斗争近期变得更加明显。凭借其超民族主义和激进的态度，此人已在社区成员中制造了许多冲突。

哈森科赫尔（Hasencohrl）先生，德国国家社会主义党远东专员，于1934年5月6日抵达上海，试图调和两派的观点，但因缺乏必要的权威而未获成功。

由于哈森科赫尔先生的失败，争斗变得更加激烈。哈森科赫尔先生逐渐受到极端分子的影响，随后他遭遇了

pages.en:
- 2 -

still more violent opposition on the part of "the ancients".
Such was the situation at the moment of the arrival
in Shanghai, on June 21, of Lieutenant Colonel Von Kriebel,
the newly appointed German Consul-General in Shanghai, and
a personal friend of Hitler.
Being fully aware of the seriousness of the situation
Mr. Von Kriebel decided to take appropriate measures.
At this juncture the political events of June 30 took
place in Germany. They produced a great impression in
the ranks of the German community, particularly amongst
"the ancients", who at that moment were scared of the
possibility of the power being seized by the radicals.
Seizing this opportunity, Lieut-Colonel Von Kriebel
convened a general meeting of members of the German community
on July 2 in the premises of the German Garden Club. Mr. Von
Kriebel read out telegrams received from Berlin by the local
German Consulate-General and endeavoured to pacify excited
minds by declaring that everything was going for the better
in the Reich. At the same time he warned certain "noisy
elements" of the local German community that he would take
all necessary measures, should those elements attempt to
carry on any agitation in Shanghai.
Enquiries instituted by Lieut-Colonel Von Kriebel
regarding the origin of the dissensions among the local
German community led to the following conclusions:-
The major part of the responsibility for these
dissensions rests with the extremist group of the local Nazi,
who by their arrogant attitude and their desire of power
discouraged advances made by the moderate and influential
elements of the local German community. This group of
extremists has actually succeeded in terrorizing their
fellow citizens. For this reason Mr. Von Kriebel intends
pages.zh:
- 2 -

来自“老派”更为激烈的反对。
6月21日，新任德国驻上海总领事、希特勒的私人朋友冯·克里贝尔中校（Lieutenant Colonel Von Kriebel）抵达上海时的局势即是如此。
冯·克里贝尔先生充分意识到局势的严重性，决定采取适当措施。
值此之际，德国发生了6月30日的政治事件。这在德国社区各阶层，特别是“老派”中产生了巨大影响，当时他们担心权力可能被激进分子夺取。
冯·克里贝尔中校抓住这一机会，于7月2日在德国花园俱乐部（German Garden Club）召集了德国社区成员大会。冯·克里贝尔先生宣读了当地德国总领事馆从柏林收到的电报，并宣布帝国内一切都在向好发展，试图安抚激动的人心。同时，他警告当地德国社区中某些“喧闹分子”，如果这些人试图在上海进行任何煽动活动，他将采取一切必要措施。
冯·克里贝尔中校针对当地德国社区分歧起源进行的调查得出了以下结论：
这些分歧的主要责任在于当地纳粹的极端主义群体，他们以傲慢的态度和对权力的渴望，阻碍了当地德国社区中温和且有影响力成员所做的努力。这个极端主义群体实际上成功地恐吓了其同胞。因此，冯·克里贝尔先生打算

pages.en:
- 3 -

at present to carry out a complete reorganisation of the
Shanghai Branch of the German National Socialist Party
within 4-5 months.

Certain drastic measures have already been announced.
For instance, the local branch of Nazi will in future be
allowed to occupy themselves only with questions relating
to the party affairs.

Any interference on the part of the local branch of
Nazi with the Reich's politics in the Far East, with economic
questions, as well as with questions relating to the German
community as a whole is strictly forbidden. These questions
will remain within the competence of the German Consul-General
in Shanghai and of a Special Council, members of which will
be appointed by the Consul-General.

Members of this Special Council will be chosen from
representatives of various classes of the local German
community. The fact of being an adherent of the German
National Socialist Party will not play any role in the
matter of making these appointments.

At the same time a purification of the party will
be carried out. Certain measures have already been taken,
and as a result of this purification several influential
members of the local branch of Nazi have been excluded.

Mr. Eckhusen, former editor of the "Far Eastern Observer"
("Ostasiatischer Beobachter"), official organ of the local
branch of Nazi, has been dismissed and recalled to Germany.
His successor is Dr. Finkeldey, professor of the Tung Chi
University. Similar measures were taken against Mr. Link,
secretary and the "right hand" of Captain Hennig, head of
the local branch of the German National Socialist Party, who
pages.zh:
- 3 -

目前在4-5个月内对德国国家社会主义党上海分部进行全面重组。

某些严厉措施已经公布。例如，纳粹当地分部今后只允许处理与党务有关的问题。

严禁纳粹当地分部干涉帝国在远东的政治、经济问题以及涉及整个德国社区的问题。这些问题将保留在德国驻上海总领事和特别委员会的职权范围内，特别委员会成员将由总领事任命。

特别委员会成员将从当地德国社区各阶层的代表中选出。是否为德国国家社会主义党信徒在这一任命过程中不起任何作用。

同时，将对党进行清洗。已采取某些措施，作为此次清洗的结果，纳粹当地分部的几名有影响力的成员已被除名。

《远东观察家》（"Ostasiatischer Beobachter"）前编辑埃克胡森（Eckhusen）先生，该报是纳粹当地分部的官方机关报，已被解职并召回德国。其继任者是同济大学教授芬克尔代博士（Dr. Finkeldey）。针对林克（Link）先生也采取了类似措施，他是德国国家社会主义党当地分部负责人亨尼格上尉（Captain Hennig）的秘书及“右臂”，他

pages.en:
- 4 -

has been replaced by Mr. Kuck, professor of the German
School (Great Western Road). Mr. Rambow, Chief of the
Information Bureau of the local branch of Nazi, and Mr.
Schmidt, of Melchers & Co., former secretary of the local
branch of Nazi, have also fallen in disgrace and were
replaced by Mr. Groesser, exchange broker, and Mr. Klein,
of the firm of "Ganzmann Co." respectively.

Discreet enquiries have been instituted regarding
activities of Mr. H. Becker (Hamburg-America Line), former
head of the local branch of the German National Socialist
Party, and Mr. K. Flamme (Deutsche Farben Handelsgesellschaft)
whose "radical nationalism" seems to have been too conspicuous
of late.

Finally, Mr. Kellner of the firm "Reuter, Brockelmann
& Co." has been expelled from the party for "want of delicacy"
in respect of his employers. Upon his refusal to return to
Germany, the case against him was brought before the First
Special District Court of Shanghai.

It is to be noted that there is in Shanghai another
group of Germans, which is of little importance and hostile
towards Hitler. This group, headed by Th. Eckhardt, editor
of the "China Dienst", German Economic Review, published in
Shanghai, represents in our city the review entitled "The
Ring" (Der Ring), an official organ of the "Club of Gentlemen"
("Herrenclub") in Berlin.

The "Club of Gentlemen" consists of high officials,
military officers, bankers and industrialists representing
in Germany the interests of the liberal capitalist and
industrial circles which ruled the Reich from 1924 to
January 30, 1933. It is the party to which General Schleicher
belonged who met a tragic death at the time of events of
June 30.

已由德国学校（大西路）教授库克（Kuck）先生接替。纳粹党当地分部情报局局长兰博（Rambow）先生，以及美最时洋行（Melchers & Co.）的施密特（Schmidt）先生（前纳粹党当地分部秘书），也已失势，并分别由外汇经纪人格罗瑟（Groesser）先生和“甘兹曼公司”（Ganzmann Co.）的克莱因（Klein）先生接替。

已就汉堡-美洲航运公司（Hamburg-America Line）的贝克尔（H. Becker）先生（前德国国家社会主义党当地分部负责人）以及德意志染料贸易公司（Deutsche Farben Handelsgesellschaft）的弗拉梅（K. Flamme）先生的活动展开审慎调查，此二人的“激进民族主义”近期似乎过于引人注目。

最后，鲁特·布罗克尔曼公司（Reuter, Brockelmann & Co.）的凯尔纳（Kellner）先生因对雇主“缺乏分寸”而被开除出党。由于他拒绝返回德国，针对他的案件已被提交至上海第一特区地方法院审理。

值得注意的是，上海还有另一个德国人群体，其影响力微乎其微且对希特勒持敌对态度。该群体由在上海出版的德文经济评论《中国服务》（China Dienst）编辑埃克哈特（Th. Eckhardt）领导，在本市代表名为《环》（The Ring / Der Ring）的刊物，该刊物是柏林“绅士俱乐部”（Herrenclub）的官方机关报。

“绅士俱乐部”由高级官员、军官、银行家和工业家组成，他们在德国代表自由资本主义和工业界的利益，这些阶层曾于1924年至1933年1月30日期间统治帝国。施莱谢尔（Schleicher）将军所属的即是该派系，他在6月30日事件中遭遇不幸身亡。

Report No. 572/3

Subject: Internal strifes in the local German Community.
References: Activities of Foreign Political Groups in Shanghai.

Since the time of Hitler's coming into power, the local
German community has been divided into two groups: a group
consisting of persons who have accepted the new regime, but
were still impregnate with the ideas of the past, and a group
composed of 100% partisans of the new regime.

The former group, which may be referred to as "the
ancients", consists mainly of the moderate and influential
elements of the local German community including German
business men.

The opposing group is composed of the local branch of
the German National Socialist Party and also includes all
extremist elements, such as: representatives of the younger
generation, and majority of members of the Storm Troops
("Sturm Abteilungen").

It was the latter group, which, in the beginning of 1934,
led a furious struggle against "the ancients" in order to take
control not only of the political life of the German community,
but also in order to meddle with questions of social and economic
order, presenting interest for Germany or Germans.

The struggle became more pronounced recently, after Mr.
Hannig had taken over the leadership of the local branch of
the German National Socialist Party. By his ultra-nationalist
and radical attitude this individual has already created many
conflicts amongst members of the community.

Mr. Hasenoehrl, Commissary of the German National
Socialist Party in the Far East, who arrived in Shanghai on

报告第 572/3 号

主题：当地德国社区内部的纷争。
参考：上海外国政治团体的活动。

自希特勒掌权以来，当地德国社区分裂为两个群体：一个群体由接受新政权但仍深受过去思想影响的人组成，另一个群体则由新政权的百分之百支持者组成。

前者群体可称为“老派”，主要由当地德国社区中温和且有影响力的成员组成，包括德国商人。

对立群体由德国国家社会主义党当地分部组成，还包括所有极端分子，例如：年轻一代的代表，以及冲锋队（Sturm Abteilungen）的大多数成员。

正是后一群体在1934年初发起了一场激烈的斗争，反对“老派”，旨在不仅控制德国社区的政治生活，还干涉涉及德国或德国人利益的社会和经济秩序问题。

最近，在汉尼格（Hannig）先生接管德国国家社会主义党当地分部的领导权后，这场斗争变得更加激烈。此人以其超民族主义和激进的态度，已在社区成员中制造了许多冲突。

德国国家社会主义党远东专员哈森厄尔（Hasenoehrl）先生于

pages.en:
- 2 -

May 6, 1934, endeavoured to reconciliate the views of the
two parties, but was not successful in this as he did not
possess the necessary authority.

As a result of Mr. Hasenoehrl's failure the strifes
became more intense. Mr. Hasenoehrl gradually fell under the
influence of the extremists, following which he encountered a
still more violent opposition on the part of "the ancients".

Such was the situation at the moment of the arrival
in Shanghai, on June 21, of Lieutenant-Colonel Von Kriebel,
the newly appointed German Consul-General in Shanghai, and
a personal friend of Hitler.

（批：* See also
Fil. 10 816）
Being fully aware of the seriousness of the situation
Mr. Von Kriebel decided to take appropriate measures.

At this juncture the political events of June 30
took place in Germany. They produced a great impression in
the ranks of the German community, particularly amongst "the
ancients", who at that moment were scared of the possibility
of the power being seized by the radicals.

Seizing this opportunity, Lieut-Colonel Von Kriebel
convened a general meeting of members of the German community
on July 2 in the premises of the German Garden Club. Mr. Von
Kriebel read out telegrams received from Belin by the local
German Consulate-General and endeavoured to pacify excited
minds by declaring that everything was going for the better
in the Reich. At the same time he warned certain "noisy
elements" of the local German community that he would take
all necessary measures, should those elements attempt to
carry on any agitation in Shanghai.

Enquiries instituted by Lieut-Colonel Von Kriebel
regarding the origin of the dissensions amongst the local
German community led to the following conclusions:-
pages.zh:

1934年5月6日抵达上海，试图调和两派的观点，但由于缺乏必要的权威而未获成功。

由于哈森厄尔先生的失败，纷争变得更加激烈。哈森厄尔先生逐渐受到极端分子的影响，随后遭到了“老派”更强烈的反对。

这就是6月21日新任德国驻上海总领事、希特勒的私人朋友冯·克里贝尔（Von Kriebel）中校抵达上海时的局势。

（批：* 另见
档案 10 816）
冯·克里贝尔先生充分意识到局势的严重性，决定采取适当措施。

就在此时，德国发生了6月30日的政治事件。这在德国社区内部，特别是在“老派”中产生了巨大影响，他们当时担心权力可能被激进分子夺取。

冯·克里贝尔中校抓住这一机会，于7月2日在德国花园俱乐部（German Garden Club）召集德国社区成员举行全体会议。冯·克里贝尔先生宣读了德国驻上海总领事馆从柏林收到的电报，并宣布帝国境内一切都在向好的方向发展，试图平息激动的情绪。同时，他警告当地德国社区中的某些“喧闹分子”，如果这些人试图在上海进行任何煽动活动，他将采取一切必要措施。

冯·克里贝尔中校就当地德国社区分歧起源进行的调查得出了以下结论：-

The major part of the responsibility for these
dissensions rests with the extremist group of the local Nazi,
who by their arrogant attitude and their desire of power
discouraged advances made by the moderate and influential
elements of the local German community. This group of
extremists has actually succeeded in terrorizing their
fellow citizens. For this reason Mr. Von Kriebel intends
at present to carry out a complete reorganisation of the
Shanghai branch of the German National Socialist Party
within 4-5 months.

Certain drastic measures have already been announced.
For instance, the local branch of Nazi will in future be
allowed to occupy themselves only with questions relating
to the party affairs.

Any interference on the part of the local branch of
Nazi with the Reich's politics in the Far East, with economic
questions, as well as with questions relating to the German
community as a whole is strictly forbidden. These questions
will remain within the competence of the German Consul-General
in Shanghai and of a Special Council, members of which will
be appointed by the Consul-General.

Members of this Special Council will be chosen from
representatives of various classes of the local German
community. The fact of being an adherent of the German
National Socialist Party will not play any role in the
matter of making these appointments.

At the same time a purification of the party will
be carried out. Certain measures have already been taken,
and as a result of this purification several influential members
of the local branch of Nazi have been excluded.

Mr. Eckhusen, former editor of the "Far Eastern
Observer" ("Ostasiatischer Beobachter"), official organ of
the local branch of Nazi, has been dismissed and recalled to

这些分歧的主要责任在于当地纳粹党的极端主义群体，他们以傲慢的态度和对权力的渴望，阻碍了当地德国社区中温和且有影响力成员的主动接触。这个极端主义群体实际上已经成功地恐吓了他们的同胞。因此，冯·克里贝尔先生目前打算在4-5个月内对德国国家社会主义党上海分部进行全面重组。

某些严厉措施已经公布。例如，今后纳粹党当地分部只允许处理与党务有关的问题。

严禁纳粹党当地分部干涉帝国在远东的政治、经济问题以及涉及整个德国社区的事务。这些问题将保留在德国驻上海总领事和特别委员会的职权范围内，特别委员会成员将由总领事任命。

特别委员会的成员将从当地德国社区各阶层的代表中选出。是否为德国国家社会主义党信徒在这一任命过程中不起任何作用。

同时，将进行党内清洗。某些措施已经采取，作为这次清洗的结果，几名当地纳粹分部的有影响力成员已被除名。

《远东观察家》（Ostasiatischer Beobachter，当地纳粹分部的官方机关报）前编辑埃克胡森（Eckhusen）先生已被解职并召回

Germany. His successor is Dr. Finkeldey, professor of the
Tung Chi University. Similar measures were taken against
Mr. Link, secretary and the "right hand" of Captain Hannig,

Party, who has been replaced by Mr. Kuck, professor of the

Discreet enquiries have been instituted regarding

It is to be noted that there is in Shanghai another

Germany the interests of the liberal capitalist and industrial

NAZI LEADER IS DUE
HERE TO-DAY
Mr. F. X. Hasenochrl Now
Commissioner For
The Far East ,

Mr. F. X. Hasenochrl, the Far
Eastern Commissioner of the Ger-
man National Socialist Party, is
due to arrive at Shanghai, to-day
by the m.s. Ruhr. The arrival
of Mr. Hasenochrl will be a power-
ful stimulus to the successful work
which the Nazi groups in the Far
East have been carrying out since
over two years.
Mr. Hasenochrl was born in
Vienna on August 2, 1891. After
having received training at a mili-
tary academy, he became an officer
in the Austrian army, in which he
fought during the World War. Hav-
ing been wounded several times and
after receiving a number of decora-
tions, F. X. Hasenochrl was taken
prisoner on the Russian front and
placed in a camp in Siberia.
After the war he came to China,
where he was manager of a Ger-
man firm in Hankow and later in
Shanghai. Here he took part in
the foundation of the local National
Socialist organization. At the re-
quest of his friends he took over
the leadership of the Nazi group.
Soon after, he was appointed re-
presentative of the China Section
and later of the Far Eastern Sec-
tion of the party.
In March, 1933, Mr. Hasenochrl
returned to Germany, where he
witnessed the rise of the new Ger-
many and attended the Party Con-
gress at Nuremberg in September
1933. His outstanding personality
and large knowledge of conditions
in the Far East soon made him
one of the foremost figures of the
Nazi Party organization abroad.
At the end of last year he was
appointed Far Eastern Commis-
sioner.
Mr. Hasenohrl will later visit
the party groups in North China.
—Contributed.

今日抵达
F. X. 哈森厄尔先生现任
远东专员，

德国国家社会主义党远东专员 F. X. 哈森厄尔（F. X. Hasenochrl）先生，预计今日乘“鲁尔”号轮船抵达上海。哈森厄尔先生的到来，将有力地推动纳粹团体在远东地区过去两年多来所开展的成功工作。
哈森厄尔先生于1891年8月2日出生于维也纳。在军事学院接受培训后，他成为奥地利军队的一名军官，并在世界大战期间参战。在多次负伤并获得多项勋章后，F. X. 哈森厄尔在俄罗斯前线被俘，并被关押在西伯利亚的一个营地中。
战后他来到中国，先在汉口一家德国公司担任经理，后来在上海任职。在此期间，他参与了当地国家社会主义组织的创立。应朋友们的请求，他接管了纳粹小组的领导权。不久之后，他被任命为该党中国分部代表，随后又担任远东分部代表。
1933年3月，哈森厄尔先生返回德国，见证了新德国的崛起，并出席了1933年9月在纽伦堡举行的党代会。他杰出的人格魅力和对远东局势的深入了解，很快使他成为纳粹党海外组织中的首要人物之一。去年年底，他被任命为远东专员。
哈森厄尔先生稍后将访问华北地区的党组织。

With the departure for Germany on September 12, 1933 of
Mr. F. Halbekann, former leader of the local Nazi organization,
certain differences arose between the young and elderly adherents
of Hitler in Shanghai, with the result that Mr. Georg SCHINK, a
well-known local auditor and accountant, whose offices are
situated at No. 120 Nanking Road, was placed in charge of the
Party's affairs here.
Mr. H. ECKHUSEN, the youthful secretary of the Shanghai
Nazi group, is shortly being sent back to Germany by his employers
Messrs. Carlowitz & Co. who allege that he is spending too much
time interesting himself in political problems, with the result
that his business affairs are suffering to the detriment of the
firm. This is a case that is paralleled in every respect
with that of Mr. Halbekann, whose business went to rack and
ruin following upon the time he devoted to Nazi interests
and neglected his own affairs. He also was sent back to
Germany.
Another very important change in the local Nazi orga-
nisation is the recent enlarging of the number of members from
200 to 300. By judicious methods employed by the original
elderly members of the movement, the great majority of the
extra 100 members enrolled have also been gentlemen who are

Nazis now hold the balance of power over what they themselves
term the "youthful hotheads."

organisation is that Shanghai is far from being an ideal city
in which to put into practice the tenets of Nationalist-Socialism
as they are at present carried out in Germany. They state

上海纳粹小组的年轻秘书 H. ECKHUSEN 先生，即将被其雇主卡尔洛维茨公司（Messrs. Carlowitz & Co.）遣返德国，该公司声称他在政治问题上花费了太多精力，导致其业务事务受损，进而损害了公司的利益。这一情况与哈尔贝坎（Halbekann）先生的案例完全平行，后者因致力于纳粹事务而忽视了自己的业务，导致生意破产。他也同样被遣返回德国。
当地纳粹组织的另一个非常重要的变化是，最近成员人数从200人增加到了300人。通过该运动原有的年长成员所采用的审慎方法，新招募的100名额外成员中，绝大多数也是年长的绅士。由于这一举措，“年长”的纳粹分子现在掌握了他们自己称为“年轻热血分子”的权力平衡。

are
1. Observe the laws of the country in which you/a guest.
2. The policy of the country in which you are a guest is
the business of the inhabitants of that country, not

You have not to interest your-self in the internal

get yourself involved, not even slightly in any country

3. Wherever you may be, confess you are a member of the Party.
4. Conduct yourself and speak in a manner that will reflect
honour on the National Socialist movement and likewise
New Germany. Be just, honourable, fearless and true.
5. Recognize in every German abroad your own countryman,
your kith and kin, your own race and of your own nature.
Extend to him your hand without considering his social
status. We are all workers for our own people.
6. Should any of your countrymen get into trouble and be
innocent, extend to him your heartfelt help without
being asked.
7. Be not only a member of the Party, but also a fellow-
combattant in the first line. Be properly informed of
the nature, contents and object of our movement.
8. Enlist and fight day by day for the enlistment in our
movement of every honest German. Convince him of the sup-
eriority and righteousness of our cause, of the necessity
of our victory and that Germany cannot die.
Fight with your brains.
9. Read our Party organ, our publications and books.
10. Unite your Party members in the place of your residence.
Wherever a branch or center of our Party may be, show
yourself a disciplined and active co-worker. Do not
start any trouble, but endeavour with all your strength
to smooth over all discord.

BE PROUD YOU ARE A GERMAN. BE ESPECIALLY PROUD YOU
ARE A GERMAN NATIONAL SOCIALIST!

来自德国社区各界的加入纳粹组织的申请大量涌入，因为当地所有阶层的日耳曼人都意识到，随着希特勒的机器如今稳固建立，与纳粹结盟即是保护自身利益。值得注意的是，许多在两月前还对这一运动持极度贬低态度的德国人，现在改变了说法，变得非常亲纳粹。然而，由于上海允许的成员上限仅为200人，许多申请必然会被拒绝。

由约五十名成员组成的冲锋队正在重组过程中，但其模式不同于德国的同类团体，后者处于严格的军事管制之下。当地的冲锋队将按照体育和运动部门的方式运作，以便其成员进行游戏并与其他俱乐部竞争。他们仅在当地的特殊场合穿着其特色制服，该制服外观上与德国冲锋队所穿的制服非常相似。

截至目前，当地德国总领事馆的人员尚未发生变动，但这里的纳粹分子确信地等待着预计在未来两三个月内发生的此类变动。较年长的官员

Memorandum on the Shanghai Branch of the Nazi Party.

A Branch of the "Nationalsozialistische Deutsche
Arbeiterpartei" or as it is better known the "Nazi Party"
has been in existence in Shanghai since 1929. It has
branches in Canton, Hongkong, Nanking, Tsinanfu, Tsingtao,
Harbin, Mukden, Osaka and Kobe. As far as can be
learned the aims of the members of the Nazi Party in
Shanghai and other parts of the Far East are :-
1. To teach and instruct all German Nationals in the
tenets and beliefs of Nationalist-Socialism, and to
explain to them the means whereby Hitler hopes to again
make Germany one of the Great Nations of the world.
2. To instil into the minds of all Germans a patriotic
fervour which will eventually lift their Fatherland
from the slough of despond in which for many years it
has lain, economically rotting, and to build up
the Third Reich into an all powerful National State.
3. To teach Germans to refrain from meddling in the
politics and the affairs of countries in which they are
but guests; i.e. the Germans in the Far East are
forbidden by the Nazis from participating in the
activities - official activities - of the Chinese,
White Russians, Koreans or Japanese.
4. To teach all Germans to become "open-minded" and not
to become entangled in anything of a secret nature,
no matter what it might be.
The local followers of Hitler seem to believe that it is
impossible for German Jews to adopt themselves to their
line of thinking and politics, so they are purposely
excluded from the Germans whom the Nazis try to influence.
The general trend of the opinions of local Nazis is also
said to be anti-Semitic.

“国家社会主义德意志工人党”（Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei），即更广为人知的“纳粹党”，的一个分部自1929年以来一直存在于上海。它在广州、香港、南京、济南府、青岛、哈尔滨、沈阳、大阪和神户设有分部。据所知，上海及远东其他地区的纳粹党成员的目标如下：-
1. 向所有德国国民传授和指导民族社会主义的教义和信仰，并向他们解释希特勒希望借此使德国再次成为世界大国之一的手段。
2. 向所有德国人灌输爱国热情，最终将其祖国从多年来陷入的经济腐朽的绝望泥潭中拯救出来，并将第三共和国建设成为一个全能的民族国家。
3. 教导德国人不要干涉他们作为客居者的国家的政治和事务；即，纳粹禁止远东的德国人参与中国人、白俄人、朝鲜人或日本人的活动——官方活动。
4. 教导所有德国人变得“思想开放”，不要卷入任何具有秘密性质的事情，无论其性质如何。
希特勒的当地追随者似乎认为，德国犹太人不可能适应他们的思维方式和政治路线，因此他们故意将犹太人排除在纳粹试图影响的德国人之外。据说当地纳粹分子的舆论总体趋势也是反犹的。

Although some suggestions have been put forward in
Nazi circles that local Jews suspected of hostility
should be drastically dealt with, there is no indication

THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR

By A. W. BEAUMONT

NAZI DAMN SPECTATOR

Dr. Leber, on the First of May celebrations at the Shanghai German School, celebrated the event in proper Hitlerite fashion by making a fiery speech in the interests of the Social-Democratic Party. So far so good, every man is entitled to his beliefs. Than Dr. Leber (who we are informed on good authority holds a doctorat-es-veterinary) said: "Wherever you scratch the Russian, you will discover the Jew; the Jews are all Communists and more blah of this order. Then, continued Dr. Leber, there is a paper in this town who is carrying on a campaign against us... It is the Shanghai Spectator as you all know," or gords to that effect." We must all get together and fight this......." Well, Dr. Leber, the Shanghai Spectator will be waiting......

Then followed some further vitriolic attacks in good Social Democratic fashion and the Russians were honored with a particular fine oratorical trouncing. All this is no concerns of ours, and we don't give a hang, but it is interesting to note that Dr. Leber was introduced to the gathered German community by none other than the acting German Consul General, Mr. Behrend, who once used to be German consul in Soerabaya, and who should know better. Dr. Leber also protested violently against the Spectator's publication in its last issue of a Nazi cruelty picture and stated most emphatically that this picture was a pure fabrication. It is strange, indeed, if this be true, that this same picture was also published in London's Daily Mirror issue of March 15th with a legend similar to ours.

Anyhow, Dr. Leber and his party have not succeeded in running the British Parliament yet and they are also not running the Shanghai Spectator, nor Shanghai.

Believe it or not, Dr. Leber.

JEWS DAMN SPECTATOR

In September we published a few paragraphs dealing with Tsingtao. We committed the crime of passing a few remarks that some sons and daughters of Israel did not find to their liking. Dutifully, N. E. B. Ezra, editor of the local Jewish Organ, Israel's Messenger, set out to castigate us unceremoniously, buried us, and further predicted that there was no room for us in Heaven. Below we are quoting from Israel's Messengers' October issue:

Dislike of the unlike has always been the stumbling-block of petty-minded men. The criticism of the Shanghai Spectator reflects the mind of a critic who has been swayed to believe (when studying in his Sunday Bible Classes) that the "children of Israel" are responsible for every evil under the sun, and that it would pay to nag at them whenever an opportunity occurs. Probably the Shanghai mind was thinking that he was doing a good act in attacking those whom he thinks are "inferior" to him! The medieval mind is always restless. It can see nothing good in others. It holds firmly to the belief that "He that believeth in me shall be saved; he that believeth not shall be damned." To our mind, the Shanghai Spectator betrays lack of good taste when it flays "the children of Israel" for indulging "on the hot sands" and crossing the modern "Red Sea" in beautiful Tsingtao. We fancy the Editor of the Spectator swearing by his beard not to visit the latter port. He may conquer this wish of his but then what next? Will he be able to stand passive and listen?:—

Here lies the Editor of the Shanghai Spectator
A keen manipulator
Who to heaven might have gone
If he had shone
But didn't, when he heard the news
That the place was run by Jews.

It gives us great pleasure to place this chef-d'oeuvre of literature and poetry next to Dr. Leber's blast and we believe both paragraphs speak for themselves.

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, APRIL 13, 1933

Local Leaders
Of Jews, Nazis
State Views

Halbekann Ridicules
Persecution Charges,
Says Reich Cleansed

Ezra Says German Jews
Will Fight For Rights

A Germany free from Communism and cleansed after nearly 14 years of corruption was pictured yesterday by Mr. S. Halbekann, Far Eastern chairman of the National Socialist party, in answering the charges of local Jewish leaders that Germany is "a nation run amok."

The beginning may be traced from the immigration of large numbers of low-type Jews, financial adventurers from the Eastern countries, who, finding Germany easy prey in her weakened condition, spread their influence by various means until they had assumed complete control of Parliament, the courts and even the schools. Mr. Holbekann said. Instances were mentioned in which unscrupulous ignorant Jewish immigrants rose to places of high position, subsequently enriching the coffers of international Jewry and bringing the country into a state of chaos. In Berlin alone, he stated, 60 per cent of the legal professions was composed of Jews, and allied professions were usurped to the exclusion of other races. "The Nazi program may be interpreted as simply a restoration to power of responsible men, and independence to Germany," Mr. Halbekann added.

Many Served Germany

"It is true," the Nazi official continued, "that a small number, perhaps 100,000, Jews were in the country previous to the war, and that many of these were brave, honest citizens who served our country well. These are not included in the general indictment as stated by Mr. Hitler, and are not being in any way disturbed."

Charges of physical atrocities inflicted upon the Jews were denied as being utterly unfounded by the local Nazi chief, who mention the case of the newspaper Hamburg Nachrichten, which offered a reward of 2,000 marks to any person who could bring evidence showing that a Jew had been killed or violently treated. This offer was held open for a period of about three weeks without takers and since that time has been renewed with no result.

Mr. Halbekann predicts an early end of startling propaganda of this sort, implying that this flare-up was incited by hostile foreign Jewish interests, who can in no way interrupt the careful, orderly schedule of the ruling party.

Ezra Replies

Contrary views were voiced yesterday by Mr. N. E. B. Ezra, editor of Israel's Messenger and local Jewish spokesman. "We are not going back to the Ghetto," said Mr. Ezra in reply to the Nazi statements, "and either the policy of the Hitler government will change entirely, or Jews throughout the world will move to resist this persecution to the nail. Just what retaliatory methods would be used I am unable now to say, but in Shanghai a monster meeting has been considered, and many Jews are individually boycotting German products.

"Sheer malice on their part, which I consider contemptible," he said, in speaking of the offer of the Hamburg Nachrichten. "What of Dr. Joachim, the Jewish lawyer who died on March 31 from a terrible beating administered by Hitler's cohorts? Surely one death is sufficient to claim this reward."

Communism Ridiculous

Mr. Ezra branded the charge of communism as ridiculous, stating that this contention is simply a feeble effort to throw dust in the eyes of truth. Communism, he stated, is in no way a product of the Jewish race. "We are not considering individuals now. Trotsky is a creature of his own country, our race cannot be held responsible for such men as these."

Mr. Ezra made it clear that the Jews would fight Hitler, not Germany. "Our race has lived in Germany for 1,000 years, we have built or influenced the best that is German. Her most illustrious sons have been born Jews. We will fight for our equal rights of citizenship and of the right to earn an honest living. We will not tolerate bad treatment from any nation."

埃兹拉（Ezra）称德国犹太人
将为权利而战

国家社会主义党远东主席 S. 哈尔贝坎（S. Halbekann）先生在回应本地犹太领袖关于德国是“一个失控的国家”的指控时，描绘了一个摆脱共产主义、并在近14年的腐败之后得到净化的德国。

霍尔贝坎（Holbekann）先生称，其开端可追溯至大量低劣类型的犹太人、来自东方国家的金融冒险家移居德国，他们发现虚弱的德国易于掠夺，便通过各种手段 spread 其影响力，直至完全控制了议会、法院甚至学校。他提到了一些例子，说明那些肆无忌惮、无知的犹太移民如何身居高位，随后充实国际犹太人的金库，并使国家陷入混乱状态。他指出，仅在柏林，法律从业者中就有60%是犹太人，相关职业也被篡夺，排除了其他种族。“纳粹纲领可以简单地解释为让负责任的人重新掌权，并恢复德国的独立，”哈尔贝坎先生补充道。

许多人曾为德国服务

这位纳粹官员继续说道：“确实，战前国内有少数犹太人，或许10万人，其中许多人是勇敢、诚实的公民，为我国做出了良好贡献。正如希特勒先生所言，这些人不包括在一般指控之内，也没有受到任何干扰。”

本地纳粹负责人否认了对犹太人施加身体暴行的指控，称其完全毫无根据，他提到了《汉堡新闻》（Hamburg Nachrichten）报社的案例，该报社悬赏2000马克，奖励任何能提供证据证明有犹太人被杀或遭受暴力对待的人。这一悬赏持续了约三周，无人认领，此后又再次发布，仍无结果。

哈尔贝坎先生预测此类耸人听闻的宣传将很快结束，暗示这场风波是由敌对的外国犹太势力煽动的，他们根本无法打断执政党谨慎、有序的计划。

埃兹拉的回复

《以色列信使报》（Israel's Messenger）编辑、本地犹太发言人 N. E. B. 埃兹拉（N. E. B. Ezra）先生昨日表达了相反的观点。埃兹拉先生在回应纳粹声明时说：“我们不会回到隔都（Ghetto），要么希特勒政府的政策彻底改变，要么全世界的犹太人将行动起来，抵抗这种迫害到底。目前我还无法说明将采取何种具体的报复手段，但在上海，人们已考虑举行一次大型集会，许多犹太人正在 individually 抵制德国产品。

谈到《汉堡新闻》的悬赏时，他说：“这纯粹是恶意的表现，我认为这是可鄙的。那么3月31日因遭受希特勒党羽的可怕殴打而死亡的犹太律师乔基姆（Joachim）博士呢？显然，一条人命足以领取这笔赏金。”

共产主义之说荒谬可笑

埃兹拉先生斥责有关共产主义的指控荒谬可笑，称这种论调不过是试图掩盖真相的拙劣努力。他指出，共产主义绝非犹太种族的产物。“我们现在不考虑个人。托洛茨基是他自己国家的产物，我们的种族不能为这样的人负责。”

埃兹拉先生明确表示，犹太人对抗的是希特勒，而非德国。“我们的种族在德国生活了1000年，我们建立或影响了德国最优秀的事物。她最杰出的儿子中有犹太出身者。我们将为平等的公民权和诚实谋生的权利而战。我们不容忍任何国家的恶劣待遇。”

REPORT
Date July 16, 1939
（印：CONFIDENTIAL）

Subject Arrival of Herr Georg Leicht

Made by [签名] Forwarded by D. S. I. Wittinsky

On the 15.7.39 p.m. Herr Georg Leicht, who was granted a holiday trip to Japan, by Herr Adolf Hitler, for services rendered in the cause of the Sudeten Germans during the September (1938) crisis in Eger, Sudetenland, arrived on board the s.s. "Gneisenau" in Shanghai. He was met and addressed in the name of the Party on board the ship by Herr Kunisch.

A dinner party was held in his honour, in the German Club, which was attended by the leading members of the local German community as well as a number of Sudeten Germans. Speeches were made during which Herr Lahrmann, leader of the local Group, introduced the guest of honour as a "man, who battled in the front ranks for the cause of the Sudeten Germans". Reference was made to the arrest of Herr Leicht in the "Victoria Hotel", in Eger, his subsequent release and the recognition of services rendered by Der Fuehrer.

No information as to the date of Herr Leicht's departure for Japan is at present available.

（印：机密）

主题：格奥尔格·莱希特（Georg Leicht）先生抵达

制作人 [签名] 转发人 D. S. I. 维廷斯基（Wittinsky）

1939年7月15日下午，格奥尔格·莱希特先生乘坐“格奈森瑙”号（s.s. "Gneisenau"）轮抵达上海。此前，阿道夫·希特勒先生因其在1938年9月厄格尔（Eger）、苏台德地区危机期间为苏台德德国人事业所做的贡献，批准其前往日本度假旅行。库尼施（Kunisch）先生在船上以党的名义迎接并致辞。

德国俱乐部为他举行了晚宴，本地德国社区的主要成员以及一些苏台德德国人出席了宴会。期间发表了演讲，本地小组负责人拉尔曼（Lahrmann）先生介绍这位贵宾为“一位在苏台德德国人事业前线战斗的人”。演讲中提到了莱希特先生在厄格尔“维多利亚酒店”被捕、随后获释以及元首对其服务的认可。

目前尚无关于莱希特先生启程前往日本日期的信息。
